# espalier

`espalier` turns a tree of rule modules into per-directory documentation agents
read, and into a linter that enforces the same rules deterministically.

The documents under `docs/` are the specification. Where the code and a
document disagree, the document is right — so most of the rules here check that
the two still point at each other, rather than checking style.

## Project layout

    ./
    ├─ docs/       the specification
    │
    ├─ ignores/    the ignore lists espalier ships
    │
    ├─ src/        the implementation
    │
    ├─ test/       the argument that the tool works
    │
    ├─ HANDOFF.MD  the record of what was decided and why (required)
    │
    └─ README.MD   the front page (required)

## `HANDOFF.MD` — the record of what was decided and why

Every decision that cost an argument is written down here,
struck through rather than deleted when it is superseded. A reversal that
leaves no trace is a decision that will be made again.

## `README.MD` — the front page

Opens with a level-one heading, and links into `docs/` for
anything it only summarizes. The front page is allowed to be shorter than the
specification; it is not allowed to be a second, drifting copy of it.

## Other repository paths

These paths are part of the repository but serve specific purposes outside the project layout. Use them only for the purpose stated here.

| Paths | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `node_modules/`<br>`dist/` | — |
| `.git/` | Version control metadata. `.gitignore` never lists `.git/` — git has no need to ignore itself — so this is the one exclusion no other file supplies. |
| `.gitignore` | Repository metadata. Tracked on purpose, and dictated by the tool that reads them rather than by this project's architecture. |
| `.github/` | Continuous integration. |
| `LICENSE` | Licence and legal. |
| `.claude/`<br>`.cursor/` | Editor and operating system droppings. |
| `package.json`<br>`package-lock.json` | Manifests and lockfiles. |
| `tsconfig.json` | Tool configuration. The tool decides the filename; the project only decides the contents. |
| `fixtures/**` | espalier's own fixtures are data: sixty configs, several deliberately invalid, and a root run executing all sixty is not what anyone means by it. |
| `.espalierignore`<br>`.gitignore`<br>`espalier`<br>`espalier.config.yaml` | Sources used to generate and check this repository guidance. |
| `AGENTS.MD` | Generated repository guidance; edits here will be overwritten. Modify [`ESPALIER.MD`](espalier/ESPALIER.MD) to change this document's persistent guidance. |

Every path in this directory must fit the project layout or a documented
repository-specific purpose.

## Working with Espalier

Espalier is the architecture compiler for this repository. It turns structural
rules and `ESPALIER.MD` guidance into this generated document, then checks the
working tree against them. Use it to place new code, discover the constraints on
a path, and catch architectural drift while a change is still small.

Use this loop:

1. Find the intended path in **Project layout** and read the generated guidance
   in the nearest directory.
2. Run `espalier explain <path>` when you need to understand how a path is
   governed.
3. Make the change without working around the declared structure.
4. Run `espalier lint` and follow the rule text attached to each finding.
5. Run `espalier build`, review and include any generated guidance changes,
   then run `espalier build --check` immediately before committing.

Generated guidance files are outputs, not edit targets. When a task explicitly
changes the architecture, update the corresponding `ESPALIER.MD` for guidance
or the structural rule modules for structure, then run `espalier build`.
Otherwise, if the work has no valid place or conflicts with a rule, report the
design gap instead of weakening the espalier. Use `espalier build --force` only
to restore a generated file whose provenance marker was removed; it authorizes
overwriting an unmarked document at a planned output path.
